body:
> But now the test is less specific, I mean the test could pass while the usage would not be up to date or completely broken.

That was actually the case :). The usage message was out of sync with the jsdoc that itself was out of sync with the code. Even before my feature. Still, we had a green test.

With the regexp the test is less specific (we only test that we fire a usage warning in case of bad usage, without checking the usage message), but at least this will not give us a false sense of security.

I don't think testing for a full string equality here will help us, this is just a copy-paste magnet and in the end the correctness of the usage message is not tested, we just test that this is the same string in the code and the tests.
